meanings.note: Feminine: actrice. Derived with the Romance agent/quality suffix '-eur'/'-euse' (from Latin '-or'/'-tor'). Standard masculine noun meaning 'actor'.
Stronger than aimer for things. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to love'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'adoré').

examples.text: Je suis sérieuse. J'ai toujours adoré le cinéma.
examples.trans: I'm serious. I've always loved films.

meanings.note: une agence artistique = a talent agency

examples.text: Cette agence ne représente que des stars.

meanings.note: aller + infinitive: tu vas l'agacer = you're going to annoy her
Je vais déjeuner. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to go'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'allé').
Imperative used to encourage. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to go'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'allé').

examples.trans: I'm going to have lunch twice.

meanings.note: Un grand artiste = a great artist. Masculine noun ('le artiste', plural 'les artistes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'artist'.

examples.text: Je travaille avec des artistes photographes.

meanings.note: Feminine: assistante. Masculine noun ('le assistant', plural 'les assistants') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'assistant'.

examples.text: Vous êtes l'assistante de Mathias Barneville?

meanings.note: avoir peur = to be afraid, avoir raison = to be right, avoir 40 ans = to be 40

meanings.en: helper verb of the passé composé
meanings.note: J'ai appelé = I called. French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire'). Core French verb meaning 'to have'.

meanings.en: il y a = there is, there are
meanings.note: Fixed expression. French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire'). Core French verb meaning 'to have'.
beaucoup de + noun, with no article: beaucoup de travail

meanings.en: beaucoup de = a lot of, many
meanings.note: Invariable French adverb meaning 'a lot'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

examples.trans: You know a lot of people.

examples.text: Tu connais beaucoup de monde dans le cinéma. Tu pourrais m'aider.
examples.trans: You know lots of people in film. You could help me.

meanings.note: Très bien = very well, fine. Invariable French adverb meaning 'well'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.
C'est bien. Invariable French adverb meaning 'well'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

examples.text: Très bien. Et vous? Un thé?

meanings.note: the standard greeting until evening
determiner: ce soir = tonight, cette semaine = this week
pronoun: c'est = it is; tout ce que = all that

examples.text: Je ne peux pas venir ce soir.
Cette agence ne représente que des stars.
Magali, je dois voir la pièce de Koltès cette semaine.
examples.trans: Magali, I have to see the Koltès play this week.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le cinéma', plural 'les cinémas') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'cinema'.
Masculine noun ('le cinéma', plural 'les cinémas') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'cinema'.

examples.trans: Shall we go to the cinema?

examples.text: Tu connais beaucoup de monde dans le cinéma. Tu pourrais m'aider.
examples.trans: You know lots of people in film. You could help me.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le cirque', plural 'les cirques') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'circus'.

examples.text: J'ai organisé des spectacles de cirque.

meanings.note: Masculine action/result noun formed with the Romance suffix '-ment' (from Latin '-mentum'). Prefix 'com-' (from Latin 'cum') means 'with, together'. Standard masculine noun meaning 'compliment, praise'.

examples.trans: Thank you for that nice compliment.

examples.text: Merci beaucoup pour ce joli compliment.
examples.trans: Thank you very much for that nice compliment.

meanings.note: En concert = in concert. Prefix 'con-'/'com-' (from Latin 'cum') means 'with, together'. Standard masculine noun meaning 'concert, live music show'.

examples.text: Beyoncé a fait ça après son concert.
examples.trans: Beyoncé did that after her concert.

examples.text: On va au concert ce soir.
examples.trans: We're going to the concert tonight.

examples.text: Faites-moi confiance, Audrey. Beyoncé a fait ça après son concert.
examples.trans: Trust me, Audrey. Beyoncé did that after her concert.

meanings.en: to know, to be familiar with
meanings.note: people and places; for facts use savoir

examples.trans: You know a lot of people.

meanings.note: D' before a vowel. Core French preposition meaning 'of', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.
le film de Tarantino = Tarantino's film
Also 'some': du sucre. Core French preposition meaning 'of', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.
À demain = see you tomorrow. Invariable French adverb meaning 'tomorrow'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

examples.text: Et demain, tu déjeunes avec Audiard.
examples.trans: And tomorrow you're having lunch with Audiard.

meanings.note: C'est difficile de + infinitive. Descriptive French adjective meaning 'difficult'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

meanings.en: to come in, to go in
meanings.note: Passé composé with être. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to enter'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'entré').
Polite imperative. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to enter'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'entré').

examples.text: Entrez, je vous en prie, la porte est ouverte.
examples.trans: Come in, please, the door is open.

examples.text: Elle vient d'entrer dans le bureau de Mathias.
examples.trans: She just walked into Mathias's office.

meanings.note: for (duration): ça fait des mois que j'attends = I've been waiting for months
Third-group irregular verb inherited from core Latin roots ('-ere'). Core French verb meaning 'to do, to make'.

meanings.en: faire la surprise à = to surprise
meanings.note: Third-group irregular verb inherited from core Latin roots ('-ere'). Core French verb meaning 'to do, to make'.

meanings.en: ça fait trois semaines que = it's been three weeks since
meanings.note: With time. Third-group irregular verb inherited from core Latin roots ('-ere'). Core French verb meaning 'to do, to make'.

examples.text: Ça fait une heure que j'attends.
examples.trans: I've been waiting for an hour.

meanings.note: J' before a vowel. High-frequency French pronoun meaning 'I'; clitic object forms precede the conjugated verb.

examples.text: Gabriel! Je suis à mon cours d'équitation.
examples.trans: Gabriel! I'm at my horse-riding lesson.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'pretty'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Vous êtes bien plus jolie en vrai.
examples.trans: You're much prettier in real life.

examples.text: Tes jolies petites fesses ont amorti le choc.
examples.trans: Your pretty little backside cushioned the shock.

meanings.note: definite article; l' before a vowel

examples.text: C'est le prochain film de Tarantino.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la mademoiselle', plural 'les mesdemoiselles') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'Miss'.

examples.text: Par ici, mademoiselle, s'il vous plaît.

meanings.note: merci beaucoup = thank you very much

examples.text: Merci beaucoup pour votre aide précieuse aujourd'hui.
examples.trans: Thank you very much for your valuable help today.

examples.text: Je te dis mille fois merci pour ce beau rôle!
examples.trans: I thank you a thousand times for this great role!

meanings.note: écouter de la musique = to listen to music; la musique ancienne = early music

examples.text: Elle prend des cours de musique ancienne!
Elle dit toujours: oui, j'adore la musique de Bach!
examples.trans: She always says: yes, I love Bach's music!

meanings.note: Plural nos. Spoken French det expression meaning 'our', common in natural conversation.
High-frequency French pronoun meaning 'we'; clitic object forms precede the conjugated verb.
High-frequency French pronoun meaning 'we'; clitic object forms precede the conjugated verb.

meanings.en: to organize, to arrange, to set up
meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to organize'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'organisé').

examples.trans: I want to set up a meeting.

examples.text: Si je lui dis ça, elle va organiser des manifestations!
examples.trans: If I tell her that, she's going to organise protests!

meanings.note: Invariable French adverb meaning 'yes'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

examples.text: Oui, oui. J'ai juste besoin d'un petit cours.
examples.trans: Yes, yes. I just need a little lesson.

meanings.note: Parfait! alone = great, perfect. Descriptive French adjective meaning 'perfect'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.
parler à quelqu'un = to talk to someone
Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to speak'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'parlé').

examples.text: Oui, trois cent mille. Je parle de ses vingt ans de carrière.
examples.trans: Yes, three hundred thousand. I'm talking about his twenty years of career.

meanings.en: un peu = a little, a bit
meanings.note: Peu de temps = little time. Invariable French adverb meaning 'little'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.
Peu de temps = little time. Invariable French adverb meaning 'little'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

examples.text: Oui, Cécile est un peu plus âgée.
examples.trans: Yes, Cécile is a little older.

meanings.note: French relational/descriptive adjective derived from Latin adjectival roots.

examples.text: Il y a un côté positif.
Mais il y a un côté positif.

meanings.note: before an infinitive: pour faire plaisir
+ infinitive: pour voir. Core French preposition meaning 'for', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.

examples.text: Je suis là pour voir Mathias.
C'est comme un rêve pour moi.
examples.trans: It's like a dream for me.

meanings.note: Prêt à + infinitive = ready to. Descriptive French adjective meaning 'ready'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Ils sont prêts à en discuter.
examples.trans: They're ready to talk about it.

meanings.en: to think, to think something over
meanings.note: French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire'). Prefix 'ré-' marks repetition, return, or intensity. Core French verb meaning 'to think it over'.

examples.text: Quentin a réfléchi. Il te veut vraiment.
examples.trans: Quentin has thought it over. He really wants you.

meanings.note: A play, a concert, a show on stage. Masculine noun ('le spectacle', plural 'les spectacles') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'show'.

examples.text: Le spectacle est à huit heures.
Je joue en ce moment dans un spectacle à la Porte des Lilas.
examples.trans: I'm in a show at the moment, at the Porte des Lilas.

meanings.note: Invariable French adverb meaning 'above all'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.
Invariable French adverb meaning 'above all'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

examples.text: Samuel m'a beaucoup trompée, surtout avec des actrices.
examples.trans: Samuel cheated on me a lot, mostly with actresses.

meanings.note: Tout le monde = everybody. Spoken French det expression meaning 'all', common in natural conversation.

meanings.en: tout ce que = all that, everything that
meanings.note: Pronoun use. Spoken French det expression meaning 'all', common in natural conversation.

examples.text: C'est tout ce que je peux faire.
Désolé, c'est tout ce que je peux faire.
examples.trans: Sorry, that's all I can do.

meanings.note: takes a singular verb: tout le monde est là

examples.text: On est au Westin. Tout le monde est là.
examples.trans: We're at the Westin. Everyone is here.

meanings.note: Un travail = a job. Masculine noun ('le travail', plural 'les travaux') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'work'.

meanings.en: au travail! = let's get to work!
meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le travail', plural 'les travaux') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'work'.

examples.trans: He has a lot of work.

meanings.note: travailler à Paris, travailler le dimanche

examples.text: Cannes? Tu as travaillé au festival?
examples.trans: Cannes? Did you work at the festival?

examples.text: L'un à midi, l'autre à deux heures.

je vous rappelle = I'll call you back
Place: à Paris, à mon cours. Core French preposition meaning 'at', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.
Time: à midi. Core French preposition meaning 'at', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.

meanings.en: au = à + le, aux = à + les
meanings.note: Contractions. Core French preposition meaning 'at', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.

examples.trans: She has a lot of energy.

examples.text: Je veux du mouvement, de l'action, de l'énergie!

meanings.en: to study (a subject, a period, a role)
meanings.note: étudier l'histoire = to study history

examples.text: J'ai travaillé dur pour ce rôle. J'ai étudié l'époque!
examples.trans: I worked hard for this part. I studied the period!

meanings.note: French relational/descriptive adjective derived from Latin adjectival roots.

examples.text: J'ai travaillé pour une agence événementielle.
examples.trans: I worked for an events agency.
